findings_on_new_rule: rule deliver-requested-roadside-fuel creates vehicle.fuel from nothing; elsewhere that quantity only moves between things, so it must come from a stock that loses it.

rules_written_mid_run.intent: Request roadside assistance or arrange an emergency fuel supply before continuing toward the town.

action_signature.description: Request roadside assistance to deliver one unit of emergency fuel to a stopped vehicle.

checks.label: The Delivery driver is requesting assistance
The Delivery vehicle belongs to the Delivery driver
The Delivery driver and Delivery vehicle are on the same route
The Delivery vehicle lacks fuel for ten miles

limits: The request is available only after insufficient fuel has stopped the vehicle.
Only one pending roadside-fuel request can exist for a vehicle.
The roadside provider, payment, communication method, and exact response time are omitted because they have no represented state.
The request does not itself move the vehicle or deliver fuel.
Each completed request supplies exactly one fuel unit.
rule.rationale: A driver whose owned vehicle has stopped for insufficient fuel can request a represented pending emergency-fuel delivery.
semantic_bindings: components.vehicle.operational_status equal to awaiting roadside fuel represents an accepted request whose emergency fuel has not yet arrived.
components.vehicle.fuel below 0.4 represents insufficient fuel for the modeled ten-mile driving attempt.
The selected Delivery driver accompanies the owned Delivery vehicle without consulting components.driver.road_position.
tests: A driver can request roadside fuel for an owned stopped vehicle with less than 0.4 fuel.
The request changes the Delivery vehicle status to awaiting roadside fuel without immediately changing its fuel or road position.
A request is refused while the Delivery vehicle is operational.
A request is refused when the Delivery vehicle has at least 0.4 fuel.
A request is refused when the Delivery vehicle does not belong to the Delivery driver.
A request is refused when the Delivery driver and Delivery vehicle are on different routes.

checks.label: The Delivery vehicle is awaiting roadside fuel

rule.rationale: An accepted roadside-assistance request resolves by delivering one emergency fuel unit and returning the stopped vehicle to operational status.

proposal.why: These rules let any driver request time-delayed emergency fuel for an owned vehicle stopped by insufficient fuel, after which one fuel unit arrives and the vehicle can continue.

rules_written_mid_run.ruling: No rule could be added that passes the checks; the attempt has no effect in this world.

rules_written_mid_run.intent: Attempt to request roadside assistance or a tow to transport the delivery vehicle and cargo to the town at mile 120.

action_signature.description: Request roadside assistance or a tow for a stopped delivery vehicle to an ahead destination.

checks.label: The Delivery driver is requesting roadside assistance
The Delivery vehicle belongs to the Delivery driver
The Delivery driver and Delivery vehicle are on the same route
The Delivery vehicle and destination are on the same route
The Delivery vehicle lacks fuel for ten miles
The destination is ahead of the Delivery vehicle

limits: The action records only the driver's roadside-assistance request.
No tow provider, communication system, response time, cargo state, or payment state is represented.
The request does not move, refuel, repair, or change the status of the Delivery vehicle.
The request is refused unless the Delivery vehicle is stopped with less than 0.4 fuel.
The selected destination must be ahead on the same represented route.
rule.rationale: A driver whose owned vehicle has stopped without enough fuel can request roadside assistance toward a selected destination ahead, while no unrepresented towing outcome is assumed.
semantic_bindings: components.driver.decision_status equal to awaiting roadside assistance represents a submitted request with no represented response yet.
components.vehicle.operational_status equal to stopped identifies the vehicle stranded by the existing insufficient-fuel process.
Fuel below 0.4 means the Delivery vehicle cannot complete another represented ten-mile advance.
A greater destination road position represents a destination ahead of the stopped Delivery vehicle.
The absence of represented assistance or towing resources prevents this action from asserting transport to the destination.
tests: A driver can request roadside assistance when the owned Delivery vehicle is stopped with less than 0.4 fuel and the Town is ahead on the same route.
A successful request changes the Delivery driver's decision status to awaiting roadside assistance.
A successful request does not move or refuel the Delivery vehicle.
The request is refused while the Delivery vehicle is operational.
The request is refused when the Delivery vehicle has at least 0.4 fuel.
The request is refused when the Delivery vehicle does not belong to the Delivery driver.
The request is refused when the destination is not ahead of the Delivery vehicle.
The request is refused when the destination is on a different route.

proposal.why: This adds a general request action for an owner whose vehicle has stopped without enough fuel, recording the request without inventing an assistance provider or claiming an unsupported tow outcome.

situation_briefing: A delivery driver with a quarter tank must reach a town 120 miles away; there is one gas station at mile 60.
